paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES (blue line with circle markers) and Random (orange line with circle markers)—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of length, ranging from 15.50 to 19.00) across varying numbers of in-context examples (x-axis, ranging from 0 to 8, marked at intervals of 2). The x-axis is linearly scaled with integer tick labels. The y-axis is linearly scaled, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.50 units. The ST-ES line starts at 19.00 when the number of examples is 0 and decreases to 15.50 at 8 examples, showing a consistent downward trend with minor fluctuations. The Random line starts at 18.50 when the number of examples is 0 and generally trends downward to 17.50 at 8 examples, with a slight increase near the end. Both lines show a steep initial decline followed by a more gradual change.
